title: Berry curvature dipole circuit quantum electrodynamics
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Valla Fatemi, Justin C. W. Song
abstract: Quantum three-wave mixing is an important resource in superconducting quantum circuits. The traditional implementation uses Josephson junction arrays and is activated by magnetic flux. Here we introduce the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) quantum circuit element, which achieves quantum three-wave mixing without breaking time-reversal symmetry. This quantum three-wave mixing results from the BCD nonlinear Hall effect in noncentrosymmetric quantum materials taken to a dissipationless, quantum coherent few-photon regime. We show how nonlinear Hall materials can be integrated to superconducting microwave circuits to accomplish multiphoton vacuum Rabi splittings and dynamical stabilization of bosonic Schrödinger cat states. Such BCD circuit quantum electrodynamics are a concrete exemplar of a physical resource for quantum information processing enabled by nonlinear response in quantum materials.
summary: This paper introduces the Berry curvature dipole (BCD) as a novel, time-reversal symmetry preserving mechanism to achieve quantum three-wave mixing in superconducting circuits. By utilizing noncentrosymmetric superconductors, the authors derive a nonlinear circuit Hamiltonian that can be used to engineer quantum gates. This offers a promising, material-based route for quantum information processing that bypasses limitations of traditional Josephson junction approaches.
main_problem: To introduce a novel, time-reversal symmetry (T)-preserving method for achieving quantum three-wave mixing in superconducting quantum circuits, moving beyond traditional methods that require breaking T and P symmetries.
main_result: The Berry curvature dipole (BCD) element provides an intrinsic, T-preserving mechanism for three-wave mixing, enabling the creation of nonlinear quantum circuits without Josephson junctions or external magnetic fields.
method: The analysis involves deriving nonlinear supercurrents ($\mathbf{j}_{	ext{BCD}}$) from the BCD nonlinearity in noncentrosymmetric superconductors and modeling this using a third-order Lagrangian term ($\mathcal{L}_{	ext{BCD}}$) to derive the nonlinear circuit Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the BCD quantum circuit element realized in noncentrosymmetric superconductors, sometimes specifically using a strained twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) on hBN heterostructure.
key_observables: Three-wave mixing strength ($g_3$), energy level splitting, superfluid weight, and intrinsic Kerr nonlinearities.
important_parameters: Dissipationless, quantum coherent few-photon regime ($\omega < 2\Delta_{sc}/\hbar$); BCD nonlinearity strength ($g_{	ext{BCD}}$) scaling relative to Kerr effects.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the $	ilde{\chi}_{\gamma eta-	ext{}}$ component, which is finite and dissipationless, and assumes the ability to build the circuit using noncentrosymmetric superconductors.
figures_summary: Figures compare T/P breaking vs. BCD T-preserving mixing, show minimal three-terminal circuit implementations, and illustrate the nonlinear growth of energy level splitting due to the BCD term.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the need for T-preserving mixing, deriving the BCD supercurrent and Hamiltonian, demonstrating its application in circuit QED, and finally providing detailed theoretical derivations using BdG Hamiltonians and perturbation theory to quantify the BCD and Kerr effects.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical implementation of nonlinear quantum interactions necessary for building scalable quantum processors, providing a material-based mechanism (BCD) that circumvents symmetry constraints.
